stories.headline: PSNI scales back police welfare checks
stories.body: From the start of November, police in Northern Ireland will only do concern-for-welfare checks where there is a risk to life, risk of harm or a crime, under Right Care Right Person. Some 999 calls will be passed to health, social care or other services.
stories.why: Some calls police no longer attend may be passed to health services, which matters for ambulance crews in NI.

stories.headline: National early warning score for children in A&E
stories.body: Emergency departments in England are bringing in a standard Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS), scoring vital signs so deteriorating children are escalated fast. Any concern from staff, parents or the child triggers an immediate review.
stories.why: Knowing how EDs score and escalate sick children helps make paediatric handovers sharper.

stories.headline: Fuel costs squeeze East of England air ambulances
stories.body: Magpas says fuel costs have left a £50,000 hole in its budget, about 17 missions. East Anglian Air Ambulance expects around £200,000 more a year if prices stay high, while demand is at record levels.
stories.why: Charity-funded air ambulances are a key part of prehospital care, and rising costs put that capacity under pressure.

stories.headline: LAS violence unit backs staff through 640 police cases
stories.body: London Ambulance Service's Violence Reduction Unit helps colleagues report assaults, chase stalled investigations and even get closed cases reopened. Its manager is a former crew member who was once trapped by an aggressive patient.
stories.why: If you're assaulted at work, you shouldn't have to face the reporting process alone.

stories.headline: Visually impaired call handler takes 999 calls at EMAS
stories.body: A 21-year-old with the eye condition Stargardt disease answers 999 calls at East Midlands Ambulance Service using screen-magnifying software, with his guide dog beside him. It's a first for the trust.
stories.why: Other ambulance services have been in touch about opening similar roles to visually impaired people.
